data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'murr', which means 'to guide' or 'to lead'. Marmuri is a name given to those who are considered to be the guided ones in life, leading others to the right path. The name Marmuri carries the meaning “The Guided One” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Marmuri usually hope their child will grow to embody the guided one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: Marmur ibn Malik al-Ashtar was a prominent military commander during the early Islamic conquests. He was the governor of Kufa under the Rashidun Caliphate. He was born in the city of Ashtar in Iraq, and his name is believed to mean 'the one from Ashtar'. He is known for his military campaigns against the Byzantines and the Sassanians.
